we identified and characterized 16 polymorphic loci in the NF2 region and we showed the usefulness of these markers to detect NF2 genomic deletions.
we developed 16 polymorphic microsatellite markers in NF2 genomic sequence to facilitate the deletion screening in familial studies.

the development of a set of 16 polymorphisms in the NF2 region, which will facilitate the detection of genomic deletions and the analysis of the NF2 locus in linkage studies.
the development of a molecular diagnostic test for NF2, based on the detection of genomic deletions.
the development of a rapid and accurate method to detect large genomic deletions in the NF2 locus.

the NF2 gene is a tumor suppressor gene located on the long arm of human chromosome 22, at 22q12.2, and it is composed of 17 exons spanning approximately 70 kb.
the NF2 genomic region is characterized by 16 polymorphic microsatellites and that these markers are useful for NF2 gene deletion detection.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified 16 polymorphic loci in the NF2 locus, 15 of which were used to perform hemizygosity tests in familial studies.
16 polymorphic microsatellite markers were identified in 11 introns and 5 exons of the NF2 genomic locus.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the NF2 gene is a large gene (18.5 kb) with a high density of polymorphic markers (16 markers in 18.5 kb, 0.86 markers/kb) which is very unusual for a gene.
the NF2 gene contains a high proportion of polymorphic sequences that can be used for the detection of large genomic alterations.
the 16 polymorphic NF2 markers are highly informative and can be used to detect large deletions and point mutations in the NF2 genome.
